claims.statement: EU electricity rules provide for aggregation contracts independent of supply and require demand response through aggregation to be allowed and fostered.

contrary_evidence: The same directive makes aggregators financially responsible for imbalances or requires them to delegate that responsibility.
EU-level rights do not prove that a small Polish portfolio can access a profitable local product today.

economics.acquisition_route: Partner-led energy audits and direct outreach to cold storage, light industry, gyms, and battery owners
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A possible path is a contracted portfolio large enough to produce several million PLN of annual high-margin share revenue, with value tied to durable mandates and performance data
economics.founder_time: Initially 15-20 hours per week, with installation and 24-hour operations contracted to partners
economics.gross_margin_basis: Expected 55-75% after telemetry, controls support, partner fees, and owner revenue share
economics.payback: Unknown until Polish product minimums and revenue per controllable kilowatt are confirmed
economics.pricing: Unvalidated: retain 20-30% of net flexibility and optimization proceeds, with optional 500-1500 PLN monthly monitoring fee
economics.retention_or_repeat: Two- to three-year mandates could recur if savings and settlement remain transparent

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Contracted megawatts, dispatch history, and integration templates improve market access and make the portfolio costly to replicate
fingerprint.customer: Polish SMEs with controllable electrical loads that lack the scale or expertise to monetize flexibility
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Energy auditors, refrigeration and controls contractors, the family installer network, and targeted analysis of suitable commercial sites
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Free flexibility audit, controls integration, exclusive aggregation mandate, automated scheduling, and revenue-share settlement
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A market-access partner settles delivered flexibility and the company retains 20-30% before paying the asset owner
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An owner has flexible consumption or storage but no economical route to participate in electricity flexibility markets

founder_fit: Combines data science, optimization, and renewable-energy relationships
Can begin as an orchestration layer rather than a licensed balance-responsible party
Recurring automated dispatch is compatible with system-building preferences
Polish SME access can start through the family company
risks: Imbalance exposure or penalties could exceed revenue
Remote controls create operational and cybersecurity liability
Exclusivity terms could be unfair if owners cannot exit
National implementation may restrict accessible products or asset classes

structure.control_point: Exclusive time-bounded dispatch and settlement mandates over a contracted load portfolio
structure.critical_dependency: A licensed market-access partner must accept the assets and the portfolio must meet telemetry and performance rules

thesis: Obtain exclusive dispatch, meter-data, and settlement mandates from Polish cold stores, workshops, batteries, and commercial buildings, then pool them through a licensed aggregation or balancing partner and retain a share of delivered flexibility revenue.
title: SME Flexibility Mandate Cooperative
uncertainties: Unknown current Polish aggregator onboarding requirements and minimum bid sizes
Unknown revenue density for small assets
No market-access partner or asset owner has committed
